Praise Room

App pages

Songs, a song, setlists, a setlist, folders and a folder, in the same Liquid Glass world as the public setlist view. Both frames are live: click a song or setlist to open it in the reader, and use its back button to return.

Phone portrait · 390 × 844

How the pages are laid out

  • One nav island. Home, Songs, Setlists and Folders float in a single glass capsule at the bottom.
  • A sticky top bar. The big title scrolls away into a compact title; your vinyl profile sits top right.
  • Search sticks to the top on Songs, Setlists and Folders, with filters in a sheet.
  • One floating action button above the nav island: add a song, a setlist or a folder.
  • Every set is a strip of light. One pixel per song: the accent for the next set, half-lit once played, dim while it waits. The same pixels build each folder's cover and mark the calendar.
  • A lead on every page. Home and Setlists open on the next set; Songs opens on search; played sets fold away.
  • Sheets rise from the bottom for New setlist, New folder, Add people and every ⋯ menu.

Try this

  1. Open Songs, type "grace", then open the filter and tap Slow.
  2. Open a song, switch to Chords, then tap + to add it to a setlist.
  3. In Setlists, swipe a row left, then open Sunday Service.
  4. In a folder, add people and add setlists.

Desktop landscape · 1440 × 900

Islands down the left

The brand, the pages with counts, the next set (one click from Songs and Folders), and your vinyl profile at the foot.

Pick, then open

Click a song to preview its key, tempo and first verse beside the table; double-click or press Enter to open it. Folders open beside their list, and hovering a calendar day lights its setlist.

Song and setlist reuse the reader

A song opens in the setlist view's reader on its own, with ‹ Songs, Add to setlist and Edit. A setlist opens as the setlist view with ‹ Setlists and Edit.

This is a design mock, not the production app. Changes you make (new folders, members, setlists) last until you reload.

Sample songs are public-domain hymns plus one synthetic Chinese demo song; people are dummy accounts. Icons: pixelarticons (MIT). Fonts: IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono, plus the trial pairings' Space Grotesk, Space Mono, Work Sans, JetBrains Mono, DM Sans and Open Sans (SIL Open Font License), embedded so this file works offline.
